Q1.answer: Forecasters normalized with training-set mean/std mis-scale every input after the series undergoes a level shift post-deployment; the paper asks whether normalizing each input window with its own recent statistics (RWN) removes the resulting error without hurting no-shift accuracy, and how much of any gain requires continued adaptation of the statistics.

Q2.answer: Deployed forecasters (e.g. electricity demand) encounter level shifts, and standard pipelines then feed mis-scaled inputs to the model, increasing error. It also matters to know whether that error comes from stale normalization or insufficient model capacity, since the remedies differ.
Q2.missing: Prevalence of level shifts and standard practice are asserted with [CITATION NEEDED] placeholders, so the importance is asserted rather than evidenced.

Q3.answer: According to the authors, in the evaluations they examined, normalization and model size were changed together, so the effect of stale normalization statistics could not be separated from model capacity.
Q3.missing: The gap claim carries '[CITATION NEEDED: literature search not yet run]', so no existing work is identified and the gap is unverified; existing per-window/instance normalization methods are not discussed.

Q4.answer: Generated a synthetic hourly load series (SynthLoad) with daily/weekly cycles and Gaussian noise; after one training year, added level shifts of s in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8} training SDs plus an unshifted test period. Compared baseline (training mean/std), RWN (each window normalized with mean/std of its most recent 48 steps), and RWN-fixed (stats estimated once from the first 48 post-shift steps then frozen), all with the same 64-unit MLP, 168h history, 24h horizon, same training budget, 5 seeds, reporting mean±SD MAE.

Q5.answer: Holding the model fixed and varying only normalization isolates the normalization effect from model capacity. The synthetic generator gives controlled shift magnitudes. RWN-fixed separates one-time re-estimation from continued adaptation. The window length 48 was chosen from a quick untuned trial.
Q5.missing: No rationale for synthetic-only data beyond control, for the MLP choice, or for window length 48 (an [ASK AUTHOR] placeholder remains).

Q6.answer: Baseline vs RWN at no shift and at s = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 (5 seeds each, test-period MAE); RWN-fixed ablation reported at s = 0.6.
Q6.missing: Test-period length, shift timing relative to the test period, noise level, and whether RWN-fixed was run at other s are not stated.

Q7.answer: At s = 0.6 RWN reduced MAE from 0.641 to 0.452 (~29%); across s = 0.2-0.6 reductions of 11-29% with seed spread at most 0.012; no-shift MAE 0.409±0.007 (RWN) vs 0.412±0.006 (baseline).

Q8.answer: On one synthetic series with one fixed MLP and an untuned 48-step window, per-window normalization reduces error under moderate level shifts (up to 0.6 SD) with no measurable no-shift cost, and at s = 0.6 about two thirds of the gain is obtained by re-estimating statistics once after the shift, one third by continued adaptation.

Q9.answer: No benefit at s = 0.8; no evidence on real data, larger or different models, other window lengths, or variance/seasonality shifts; capacity was held fixed, not varied, so the capacity explanation was not directly tested; ablation split is only shown at s = 0.6.

Q10.answer: A capacity-controlled synthetic comparison showing that rolling-window normalization removes much of level-shift-induced error for moderate shifts at no no-shift cost, with a boundary at the largest shift and an ablation splitting the gain between re-estimation and continued adaptation.

Q11.answer: Single synthetic generator; untuned window length; only level shifts; single small model so capacity not varied; no benefit at s = 0.8; ablation at one shift level.

Q12.answer: On synthetic data with the model held fixed, normalizing each window with its recent 48-step statistics cut MAE 11-29% under moderate level shifts at no no-shift cost, mostly via re-estimating stats after the shift; it did not help at the largest shift, and real-data validity is untested.

location.quote: after a level shift every input the model sees is mis-scaled

findings.observed: The problem (training-statistic normalization mis-scales inputs after a level shift) is stated concretely in the first paragraph and abstract.
findings.reader_struggle: Works: an adjacent-domain robustness reader immediately sees the failure mode without forecasting background.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers correctly identify the problem being solved.
findings.revision_principle: Keep the problem stated as a concrete mechanism before introducing the method.

location.quote: [CITATION NEEDED: prevalence of level shifts in deployed load forecasting]

findings.observed: Motivation is logically clear, but both factual premises (prevalence of level shifts, standard normalization practice) rest on unfilled citation placeholders.
findings.reader_struggle: A verifying reviewer cannot check how common the problem is or that training-stat normalization is the default.
findings.likely_consequence: The importance is accepted on the authors' word; an expert may doubt practical relevance.
findings.revision_principle: Ground each premise that motivates the study in a verifiable source or evidence before relying on it.

location.quote: RQ2: how much of any gain depends on continuing to adapt those statistics

findings.observed: Two explicit RQs, each answerable, and each answered explicitly in Section 3 and Discussion.
findings.reader_struggle: Works: readers know exactly what will be tested and can check each answer.
findings.likely_consequence: Clear expectation-setting and verifiable closure.
findings.revision_principle: Continue mapping each result subsection one-to-one onto a stated question.

location.quote: [CITATION NEEDED: literature search not yet run]

findings.observed: The novelty rests on a gap claim (normalization and model size changed together in prior evaluations) that the authors admit is not backed by a literature search; per-window normalization itself is not positioned against existing adaptive/instance normalization practice.
findings.reader_struggle: A domain expert asks what is new beyond a known normalization idea and cannot find the answer; the claimed controlled separation is the only novelty and its gap is unverified.
findings.likely_consequence: Expert may judge the contribution as a re-test of a known technique with an unverified framing.
findings.revision_principle: State the contribution relative to identified prior work, and make clear whether novelty lies in the method or in the controlled comparison.

location.quote: RWN normalizes each input window with the mean and standard deviation of its most recent 48 steps

findings.observed: Core design is clear, but several operational details are missing: how outputs are de-normalized under RWN, whether MAE is computed on the original or normalized scale, the timing of the shift relative to the test period, test-period length, noise level, and training budget.
findings.reader_struggle: If MAE were measured in each method's normalized space, comparisons would not be like-for-like; a verifier cannot tell. Without shift timing, it is unclear how much error comes from windows straddling the shift.
findings.likely_consequence: The comparison cannot be reproduced and its fairness cannot be confirmed.
findings.revision_principle: Specify every step that affects the metric's scale and the evaluation window, so a reader could re-run the comparison.

location.quote: Freezing the statistics after one post-shift window gave MAE 0.518 at s = 0.6

findings.observed: Shift sweep with 5 seeds is appropriate, but the RQ2 ablation appears to be run or reported at a single shift level without seed spread; only one baseline normalization is compared; one untuned window length.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot tell whether the one-third attribution is stable across shift sizes, or whether RWN beats other simple adaptive schemes.
findings.likely_consequence: The ablation split is read as general when it is a single-point estimate.
findings.revision_principle: Run the ablation over the same conditions and seeds as the main comparison, or scope its conclusion to the condition tested.

location.quote: across s = 0.2-0.6 the reduction was 11-29%

findings.observed: Only no-shift, s = 0.6 (means only) and s = 0.8 (with SDs) numbers are given; values for s = 0.2 and 0.4 and SDs at s = 0.6 are not reported in text.
findings.reader_struggle: The 11-29% range cannot be mapped to specific shifts or checked; the figure is described but its values are not available.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers accept the range without being able to verify it or see the trend.
findings.revision_principle: Report every headline number with its condition and spread in a form the reader can inspect directly.

location.quote: This is an interpretation: capacity was held constant, not varied

findings.observed: The capacity-vs-normalization interpretation is carefully hedged, but the s = 0.8 failure (RWN MAE 0.712 vs 0.409 unshifted) is not reconciled with the claim that stale statistics account for most shift-induced error; per-window normalization should in principle remove a pure level offset regardless of size.
findings.reader_struggle: An expert sees that a large residual error at s = 0.8 contradicts a pure normalization explanation and gets no account of why.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers may doubt the mechanism or suspect an unreported artifact (e.g. transition windows, variance changes).
findings.revision_principle: When a boundary result conflicts with the proposed mechanism, discuss what it implies for that mechanism rather than only noting it.

location.quote: Three further limits bound these conclusions.

findings.observed: Synthetic data, untuned window, level-shifts-only and untested capacity are disclosed and tied to claims. Not disclosed: RWN-fixed requires knowing when the shift occurred (oracle timing), and the ablation is at one shift level.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers may treat RWN-fixed as a deployable alternative and the one-third split as general.
findings.likely_consequence: Slight overreading of RQ2 practical relevance.
findings.revision_principle: Disclose every assumption of each compared condition that would not hold in deployment, and bound the claims each limit affects.

location.quote: Both answers are bounded.

findings.observed: Problem -> competing explanations -> controlled design -> RQ answers -> bounded discussion forms one consistent thread.
findings.reader_struggle: Works: each section follows from the previous one.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers retain a coherent story.
findings.revision_principle: Preserve the question-answer structure through revisions.

location.quote: a level shift of magnitude s, measured in training standard deviations

findings.observed: Level shift, RWN, RWN-fixed and s are defined at first use. The intro contribution list states 'shift levels up to 0.6' without units, and MAE scale is never stated.
findings.reader_struggle: Minor: a reader of the contributions list alone cannot interpret 0.6; MAE values lack units.
findings.likely_consequence: Small friction; no serious misreading.
findings.revision_principle: Attach units or scale to every number wherever it first appears.

location.quote: Section 2 describes the setup, Section 3 answers each question

findings.observed: Sections progress in the announced order; each result paragraph leads with the answer and then the evidence.
findings.reader_struggle: Works.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers can follow without backtracking.
findings.revision_principle: Keep answer-first paragraph structure.

location.quote: Seed spread was at most 0.012, small next to these differences

findings.observed: Several claims cannot be traced to presented numbers: the 11% end of the range, SDs at s = 0.6, the RWN-fixed spread. The 'at most 0.012' spread claim conflicts with the 0.021 and 0.015 SDs reported at s = 0.8 unless implicitly scoped to s <= 0.6.
findings.reader_struggle: A verifier cannot recompute the headline range and finds an apparent inconsistency in reported spread.
findings.likely_consequence: Reduced trust in the precision of the reported statistics.
findings.revision_principle: Make every summary statistic traceable to a reported value, and scope aggregate statements explicitly to the conditions they cover.

location.quote: Figure 1. RWN's error stays near its unshifted level for shifts up to 0.6

findings.observed: Figure 1 is referenced and captioned, but no figure or table of values is present; the caption asserts the finding rather than describing axes, and there is no table of all conditions.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers must trust the caption's claim; they cannot see the trend or error bars across s.
findings.likely_consequence: The key visual evidence for RQ1 is effectively unavailable; 'stays near' cannot be judged (0.452 vs 0.409 at s = 0.6).
findings.revision_principle: Provide the full per-condition results (figure plus a table of means and spreads, including the ablation) so the visual claim can be checked.

location.quote: An ablation attributes about a third of the gain to continued adaptation.

findings.observed: Most claims are scoped to the evidence (moderate shifts, this setting). The ablation claim in the abstract and contribution 3 is stated generally though evidence is one shift level without seed spread.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers of the abstract infer the split holds across shifts.
findings.likely_consequence: Mild overgeneralization of RQ2.
findings.revision_principle: Carry the tested condition into every restatement of a result.

location.quote: the extra error that follows a level shift appears to stem mostly from stale normalization statistics

findings.observed: Hedged, but 'mostly' is inferred without varying capacity and in the face of the unexplained s = 0.8 result; the gap claim in the intro is also unsupported.
findings.reader_struggle: An expert notices the mechanism claim goes slightly beyond a fixed-capacity comparison with a failing boundary case.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers may take the mechanism as more established than it is.
findings.revision_principle: Limit mechanism claims to what the design can discriminate, and address contrary cases before summarizing.

location.quote: Our contributions are:

findings.observed: Findings are restated in abstract, contributions, discussion and conclusion, but briefly and each with a distinct purpose.
findings.reader_struggle: Works: repetition reinforces rather than burdens in a short paper.
findings.likely_consequence: No harm.
findings.revision_principle: Keep restatements short and consistent in scope.

location.quote: Holding this model fixed is what lets differences be attributed to normalization.

findings.observed: Short, plain sentences; design choices explained with their purpose; few numbers per paragraph.
findings.reader_struggle: Works.
findings.likely_consequence: An adjacent-domain reader follows the method on one read.
findings.revision_principle: Continue pairing each design choice with its purpose.

location.quote: which answers the second half of RQ1

findings.observed: Readers are told which question each result answers and what the next section does.
findings.reader_struggle: Works.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers always know where they are in the argument.
findings.revision_principle: Maintain explicit signposting to the RQs.

location.quote: The open question is whether the same holds on real load data and larger models.

findings.observed: The takeaway (fix normalization before scaling the model) is implied but not stated as a practical implication; relevance is bounded to one synthetic setting.
findings.reader_struggle: A robustness researcher must infer what to do differently.
findings.likely_consequence: The finding is understood but its practical consequence is left implicit.
findings.revision_principle: State the actionable implication for practitioners, scoped to the evidence.

inference_issues.claim_text: An ablation attributes about a third of the gain to continued adaptation.
inference_issues.missing_link: RWN-fixed is reported only at s = 0.6, as a single mean with no seed spread; no evidence that the split holds at other shifts.

inference_issues.claim_text: stale normalization statistics, rather than model capacity, account for much of the baseline's shift-induced error
inference_issues.missing_link: Capacity was not varied (acknowledged), and the s = 0.8 case where RWN error remains ~0.71 vs 0.41 unshifted is not explained under this mechanism.

inference_issues.claim_text: In the evaluations we examined, normalization and model size were changed together
inference_issues.missing_link: No evaluations are cited; placeholder says the literature search was not yet run, so the stated gap is unverified.
Per-condition MAEs for s = 0.2 and 0.4 and standard deviations at s = 0.6 are not reported; the figure is only captioned.

inference_issues.claim_text: Seed spread was at most 0.012, small next to these differences, so the ordering held across seeds
inference_issues.missing_link: Small SD relative to mean gap does not by itself show per-seed ordering; and reported SDs at s = 0.8 (0.021, 0.015) exceed 0.012, so the statement's scope is unclear.
No comparison with other simple adaptive normalizations or a tuned window; only a static-statistics baseline is used, and the window length was untuned.

inference_issues.claim_text: The benefit vanished at the largest shift.
inference_issues.missing_link: Results section says only that a benefit cannot be claimed (gap ~1 SD, 5 seeds); 'vanished' asserts absence more strongly than the data support.

objective_discrepancies: Objective frames RQ2 as how much of any gain depends on continued adaptation generally; the paper answers it only at s = 0.6, while the abstract states the answer without that scope.

Objective asks the reader to know where the finding stops; the paper states the s = 0.8 boundary but does not explain it, so the reader knows where it stops but not why, which weakens the mechanism interpretation.
Objective does not mention the capacity-vs-normalization mechanism, but the abstract and conclusion foreground it as an interpretive takeaway.
